question: Re-fetch the published HTTP ARTA 2007.001 PDF and locate the practical-text quotation on printed/PDF page 9: does the actual paragraph still limit generalization, leaving Behistun cross-version and all-subject speech claims unverified?
source_locator: Stolper & Tavernier, ARTA 2007.001, PDF page 9 of 28 = printed page 9 (page footer 'Achemenet Juin 2007   9'): the paragraph immediately after the Gershevitch (1979: 122) quotation ending footnote 3's lead-in and before the section heading 'Old Persian tablet among the Persepolis Tablets'
source_excerpt: What is extraordinary is to find Old Persian in an administrative record, a "practical" text. It may not demonstrate general use of Old Persian, but even as an isolate it indicates wider use than previously supposed.
retrieval_method: Live re-download this pass of the exact published HTTP URL (HTTP scheme as published, not a guessed HTTPS variant) with curl --fail --location --retry 2; HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1,242,395 bytes, SHA256 c7664821696a92d968b8000bdd9ae0b61020680023f3eb29e7bb7d59f79a59f8, PDF 1.4, 28 pages (pdfinfo); download mtime 2026-10-17T18:52:09Z (local 15:52:09 -03:00). Raw PDF and extractions kept only in reports/supplement-opencode-1/scratch/round7-12-source-scribe/ (arta2007-001.pdf, arta-full.txt, arta-page9.txt); no raw PDF or full-work text is delivered in this ledger, and the excerpt is 36 words, under the 40-word cap.
basis: The refetched page-9 paragraph still limits generalization in its own wording: it identifies the tablet as an administrative record and a 'practical' text, then immediately hedges that it 'may not demonstrate general use of Old Persian', granting only 'wider use than previously supposed' as an isolate. This confirms live what the entry asserts at persia-achaemenid.md line 47 and the round-6 access-status erratum (lines 169-188): Fort. 1208-101 is a bounded counterexample to a strict display-only rule for Old Persian, not evidence of general practical or everyday use. The re-download also reproduces the parent's effective round-6 reconciliation locator (PDF/printed page 9) and file hash, so the effective partial-support disposition for S05 (parent-reconciliation R6-09-A) stands against current bytes; the round-6 worker ledger's 'pp. 5-8' attribution stays superseded, not silently repaired.
limits: Scope is one article, one page: this pass re-verifies the page-9 paragraph and the file identity only; the rest of the 28-page PDF was not re-audited in detail, and the tablet's individual Old Persian text readings are not restated here, matching the entry's deliberate restraint at line 47. The article itself presents the tablet as an isolate, so nothing here certifies Old Persian as the language of all imperial subjects, and no census of subject speech is performed. No Behistun cross-version comparison was made this pass: the DB Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian versions remain unverified against each other by this worker and the claim stays out of this ledger's scope. Hallock OIP-92 pp. 6, 42-43 remain an unre-fetched residual from round 6 (unchanged).
